answers.solution:
Solution written to **`/home/kara/solution.md`** and empirically verified.

## What the document contains

**Title / problem class** — `gitreins-tier2-criterion-requires-automated-test-evidence`.

**Root cause** — The feature was correct, but the criterion demanded *automated test evidence*. The worker produced a manual `curl` transcript + commit message, so the judge's `grep` across `*_test.go`/`*.test.ts`/`test_*.py` found nothing. Scope coupling means a from-scratch re-dispatch risks the already-passing sub-requirements and burns an attempt (a FAIL consumes an attempt; judge/parse errors don't).

**Exact fix**
1. Re-dispatch the **same worker on the same tree** with the judge finding verbatim + the unmet criterion quoted, explicitly "continue the existing tree, do not restart."
2. Add a **stdlib-only Go e2e test** (`proxy_sse_e2e_test.go`) that builds the **real proxy binary**, runs it as a subprocess pointed at a `httptest` **stub upstream on `127.0.0.1:0`**, and asserts **incremental SSE delivery** (second stub frame withheld on a channel — no timer — so a buffering artifact deadlocks and must fail).
3. Require a **falsification proof** in the same commit: sabotage → test fails → revert → green.
4. Add a **`make test-e2e`** target (plus `ci: test test-e2e`) so the suite is greppable and CI-discoverable.

**Verification** — a table of 8 checks plus acceptance criteria (re-submit same sha-scope).

## Empirical verification performed here

I extracted the document's Go test into a temp module against a minimal real proxy that forwards `/stream`:

```
gofmt clean / go vet clean
green    : --- PASS: TestProxyDeliversUpstreamSSE (0.37s)
sabotage : --- FAIL: TestProxyDeliversUpstreamSSE (30.03s)
           request real proxy: context deadline exceeded
revert   : --- PASS: TestProxyDeliversUpstreamSSE (0.43s)
```

A key correction I made during verification: an earlier draft's stub used `case <-time.After(5*time.Second)`, which let a buffering proxy *pass by racing the 5s read deadline*. The final test removes that timer so falsification is deterministic; the doc calls out this weak variant explicitly.

signatures.description: When a task criterion demands automated tests and the worker only produced a manual live proof (curl against a running service) plus a commit message saying so, the Tier 2 judge marks the criterion unmet and the verdict is FAIL even though every other sub-requirement verifies (docs, configs, build, existing unit tests all PASS). FIX LOOP THAT WORKS: (1) do NOT re-dispatch from scratch - re-dispatch the SAME worker with the judge finding pasted verbatim plus the unmet criterion quoted, telling it the tree already contains correct work ("continue the existing tree, do not restart"); (2) ask for a stdlib-only test that drives the REAL artifact as a subprocess against a throwaway stub upstream on 127.0.0.1:0, so the suite needs no live DB/service and can run in CI; (3) require a falsification proof in the same commit: sabotage the artifact so the relevant test MUST fail, show the failure, revert, re-run to green; (4) add one repo-level command (make target) so the suite is discoverable by grep/CI. ATTEMPT BUDGET: judge/parse failures consume no attempt; a FAIL does. Second pass on the same sha-scope verdict PASSED.
